subject: Mutual action plan & onramp sprint — proposed timeline and owners
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mutual action plan & onramp sprint — proposed timeline and owners

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear onramp for the 30-day evaluation. I pulled out the items we discussed and sketched a tentative sprint calendar in the attached MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_20260523.xlsx.

Top-line outcomes NebulaCorp wants (as we captured):
- Validate retrieval + reranking workflow on your infra (latency target: median < 300ms for 512-token queries)
- Verify embedding-based semantic search quality on your dataset (NDCG target: >= 0.72 on the sample eval set)
- Confirm data handling and retention meets your policy (30-day ephemeral KV cache)

Proposed 30-day cadence (high level):
- Week 0 (kickoff): environment setup, creds, baseline perf tests
- Week 1: ingestion + retrieval tests, embedding tuning sweep
- Week 2: latency optimizations, batching & caching policy, initial readout
- Week 3: hardening, failure-mode tests, mitigation runbook
- Week 4: final readout and decision workshop

Owners (Rough):
- Redwood technical lead: Karthik Iyer (runtime tuning, perf pipelines)
- Redwood PM/eng liaison: Jordan Blake (ops cadence, reporting)
- Nebula technical lead: Alex Turner (data access, infra creds)

Ask: please review the attached workbook and confirm (1) the success criteria lines, (2) whether the timeline needs to be shifted for any blocked dependencies, and (3) who from your side will join weekly check-ins (we recommend 30 minutes).

I'll put a calendar stub for kickoff next Tuesday at 10am PT unless you prefer a different slot — will send once you confirm.

Attachments: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_20260523.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nebulacorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Eval Team <eval@nebulacorp.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & onramp sprint — proposed timeline and owners

Thanks Marissa — solid writeup and appreciated the clear owners. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Success criteria — the latency target looks reasonable, but can you confirm whether the 300ms median assumes Redwood-hosted inference or our on-prem node? We need separate baselines for both.

2) Embedding quality — we'll run your sample eval but want to add a second holdout set focused on product titles (short text). Can you add that to the Week 1 plan?

3) Data retention — 30-day ephemeral KV cache is fine, but we need confirmation on audit logging for requests (S3 logs or equivalent) for compliance.

4) Weekly check-ins — I'll join the kickoff and weeks 1 and 3 readouts. I'll loop in our infra lead (Priya Rao) for Week 0 setup — her email is priya.rao@nebulacorp.com.

If those are acceptable, confirm the kickoff time and we'll get creds ready. Attached is a short compliance checklist we run on new evals (small PDF) — not required but helpful.

Best,
Alex Turner
Senior Product Manager, Data Platforms | NebulaCorp
alex.turner@nebulacorp.com

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the additional contacts. Quick notes from the infra/engineering side: 

- The 300ms median latency callout in the workbook is for Redwood-hosted inference. For Nebula on-prem we will run a separate baseline (Week 0) and include a line-item comparison in the Week 1 readout.
- I'll own the Week 0 checklist: network firewall rules, test VM credentials, model shard sizing. I'll attach a lightweight runbook (POC_RUNBOOK_v1.pdf) to this thread with the exact steps we need from your ops team.
- Regarding audit logs: Redwood can push request logs to an S3 bucket or to a customer-owned log collector. We'll need the endpoint and retention policy. Jordan, can you add a short ops ticket to the HubSpot deal to track audit-log delivery?

Next steps from my side: I will schedule a short tech-sync with Priya Rao (to confirm ports and creds) and spin up baseline containers for the hostable variant. Suggested windows: Tuesday 10–11 PT or Wednesday 9–10 PT. Alex, let me know which works.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Alex — great, thanks for the notes and for looping in Priya. Quick confirmations and the next steps I will action: 

- We will document two baseline tracks in the workbook (Redwood-hosted vs Nebula on-prem) and Karthik will own the on-prem baseline capture in Week 0.
- I'll add the short product-title holdout to the Week 1 eval plan.
- Audit logging: Karthik's team will send options (S3 vs collector) and a minimal schema by the kickoff.

Scheduling:
- Kickoff: Tue 2026-06-01 10:00 PT — I'll send a calendar invite after you confirm availability. (Tentative: 30 minutes)
- Weekly check-ins: Tuesdays 10:00 PT (Weeks 1, 2, 3) — we can collapse Week 2 into an async readout if your team prefers.
- Final readout workshop: Fri 2026-07-03 09:00 PT (1 hour) — target decision window by noon PT that day.

Action items for Alex/Priya (from Nebula):
- Confirm kickoff Tue 6/1 10:00 PT and who will be the SRE/infra attendee (Priya suggested).
- Provide access scope for ingestion sample (S3 or secure scp) and any network allowlists.

Action items for Redwood:
- Send calendar invites for kickoff + weekly cadence (Marissa).
- Post the updated workbook to the shared drive and create the HubSpot ops ticket for audit-log tracking (Jordan).

I'll attach the initial workbook and runbook again for convenience. If anything changes on your side we'll adjust timelines, but this gives both teams a tight, trackable plan.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.
Marissa
